title: Mid-turn deliveries (queued_command attachments) are ignored: typed messages and task notifications
description:
A prompt that arrives while a turn is running is not written as a user record. Claude Code
writes an `attachment` record of type `queued_command` {prompt, commandMode, origin,
timestamp}, and the parser ignores attachments.

Local history (2026-10-02): 792 such records in 114 files. In main files: 74 messages a
person typed mid-turn (never written as a normal prompt as well, so they are in no digest
and no search finds them) and 184 task notifications. In agent files: 520 task
notifications and 14 messages from the lead or the user.

Effects: typed mid-turn messages are invisible; a background agent or workflow run whose
notification arrives mid-turn keeps status open.

Change: Turn.queued lists what arrived during the turn (at, origin, text or parsed inbox);
task notifications among them feed the status logic; search, show and the web timeline
read them.
close_reason: Closed

title: Workflow agents are not discovered: transcripts under subagents/workflows/<runId>/ are skipped
description:
A colleague's session that used dynamic workflows (the Workflow tool) showed most of its
cost as "reported, not explained by messages".

Cause, from the Claude Code 2.1.287 binary (no workflow run exists in the local history to
confirm against): an agent's transcript is written to
<session>/subagents/[<subdir>/]agent-<id>.jsonl, and the subdir is set per agent; workflow
agents go under subagents/workflows/<runId>/. internal/claude/discover reads only the files
directly in subagents/ and skips directories, so every workflow agent is invisible and its
spend exists only in Claude Code's own total. The session directory can also hold
workflows/ (the persisted scripts) and remote-agents/remote-agent-<id>.meta.json (agents
that ran in the cloud: no local transcript at all).

To do:
- discover: read agent files in subdirectories of subagents/, keeping the relative path.
- model: a workflow run (run id, the Workflow tool call and turn that started it, its
  agents with label and phase); workflow agents are not started by an Agent tool call, so
  the linkage ladder has no rung for them today and they would come out unresolved.
- remote agents: list them from their meta files with cost "not available locally".
- synthetic fixture in the real layout; verify on a real workflow session (structure and
  counts only) before closing.

title: Explorer 3.2: catalog — ownership, lineage, rollups, search
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: internal/catalog — the in-memory view over all digests. PLAN.md §7. Nothing here is persisted except project.json.

- Harness-neutral: works only on model.SessionDigest. Sessions are keyed by (harness, id). Projects are grouped by the digest's project path, not by projectKey, so one project can later span harnesses.
- Load all digests from the store; Upsert(digest) and MarkMissing for incremental updates. Safe for concurrent readers with one writer.
- Ownership: a message id is billed once across all sessions. When several sessions contain the same id, the owner is decided by: explicit markers first (a session whose digest lineage says it was forked/inherited from another does not own shared messages); otherwise earliest startedAt, then earliest lastActivityAt, then smallest session id. Per session expose ownUSD (messages it owns), inheritedUSD and from which sessions.
- Lineage (PLAN.md §7; transcript-format.md §9): sessions sharing messages are linked parent → child, exposed in both directions. Each link has: sharedMessages; atTurn = index in the parent of the last turn the child copied; explicit = whether a marker (forkedFrom / session_id) says so; kind = fork when the copy carries forkedFrom or the parent has turns of its own after atTurn, continuation when the parent stops there. A copy can be partial (only the tail of the parent after a compaction).
- Families: linked sessions form a tree. Expose for any session its root, parent, children and the family's leaves (sessions nobody continues from), newest first — the leaves are the candidates to resume.
- Inherited turns: in a child, a turn whose uuid also appears among the parent's turns is inherited. Expose per session the inherited range and the first own turn. Abandoned turns (digest flag) are passed through untouched.
- Best cost per session = reported.totalUSD when present, else attributed own cost; flag exact vs estimated. Also expose attributed and unattributed (reported − attributed, when reported exists). Note for the implementer: whether a copied session's reported total includes its inherited history is not yet known (validation bead); keep the best-cost function in one place so it can be adjusted.
- Rollups: by project, by local-time day, by model, by kind, and combinations needed by the cost command (project × day, model × day). Day attribution uses each message's timestamp in the local timezone (time.Local; tests set the zone explicitly), counting only owned messages. When a session has a reported total, distribute its unattributed remainder over its days in proportion to attributed cost so day totals add up to best cost.
- Session listing with filters: project, kind (interactive | background), since/until, running. Sorted by last activity. Scripted (sdk) sessions are never returned individually by listings: they appear only as aggregate lines, one per project and day, with count and cost. They are still counted in every cost rollup.
- Search: case-insensitive, all terms must match within one field, over titles, turn userText, turn finalText, compaction summaries, project key, cwd and branch; returns session + turn index (or compaction index) + the field that matched + a snippet around the match. Ranking: title and prompt hits first, then final text, then compaction summaries; newest first within a rank. sdk sessions are never searched. A turn copied into several sessions is matched once, in the session that owns it; the hit lists the sessions that continue from it (family leaves first).
- Liveness: given the Claude sessions registry directory (<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/sessions/<pid>.json) report running busy/idle for sessions whose pid is alive; else recent (activity within 10 minutes of a supplied "now"); else ended. "now" is always passed in, never read inside the catalog.
- project.json writer: per project, the session summaries used by listings.

Out of scope: CLI formatting, HTTP.
acceptance_criteria: Tests on digests built from the fixtures: every copied-history pair is counted once in project and global totals and the child shows inheritedUSD; the five pairs are classified as the fixture README says (continuation, unmarked fork, marked fork, partial copy, SDK pick-up) with the right atTurn; family root / children / leaves are correct for a three-session family; inherited turns are identified by uuid; a prompt present in parent and child yields one search hit that names the child; rollup by day splits the day-boundary fixture at local midnight in the zone the fixture documents; sum of day rollups equals sum of best costs; listings never return sdk sessions and show the per-project-per-day aggregate line, while cost rollups include them; search finds a prompt by two non-adjacent terms and returns the right turn, finds a term that occurs only in a compaction summary and labels it as such below prompt hits, and never returns sdk sessions; liveness with a fake registry and injected pid check. Concurrent Upsert + readers under -race. make test and make vet pass.
close_reason: internal/catalog implemented: ownership, lineage/families, windows-based best cost, rollups, listing with scripted aggregates, search, liveness, project.json writer; tests on 35 fixtures + synthetic; make test, make vet, go test -race pass

comments.author: Zsolt Terek
comments.text:
COST DESIGN CHANGE (lead, after checking the real corpus) — supersedes anything in this bead that says "reported = the last cost-state record" or "best cost = reported if present else attributed".

Fact: a cost-state record is a running total for one PROCESS RUN that began at its startTime. A session therefore has one reported WINDOW per distinct startTime: from startTime to the timestamp of the last record before that window's last cost-state. Spending outside every window (before the first, between two, after the last write) is not reported at all. Inside windows the transcript-derived cost is always <= reported (about 7% under). See explorer/docs/transcript-format.md section 8 and PLAN.md sections 3 (principle 6), 5 and 7.

Schema: model.Reported now has Windows []ReportedWindow{From, To, TotalUSD, ByModel}; Reported.TotalUSD and ByModel are the sums over windows. See explorer/docs/digest-schema.md.

Rules:
- Building the digest (2.3): group cost-state records by startTime in file order. For each group: From = startTime (epoch milliseconds); To = timestamp of the last transcript record that precedes the group's LAST cost-state record in the file; TotalUSD and ByModel from that last record (model names normalised, "[1m]" stripped). If a total decreases while startTime is unchanged, start a new window there. Windows are ordered by From. The Builder's CostStateRecord needs the timestamp of the preceding record: add it additively (field At) if it is not there. linesAdded / linesRemoved in stats = sums over windows' last records.
- Catalog (3.2): a message is "covered" when its timestamp lies within a window of its session (allow 1 second of slack at both ends). bestCost(session) = Reported.TotalUSD + attributed cost of the session's OWNED messages that are not covered. Flag: exact (has windows, nothing owned is uncovered), partial (has windows and uncovered owned spend), estimated (no windows). overhead(session) = Reported.TotalUSD - attributed cost of covered messages (never negative in practice; clamp at 0 and count clamps in diagnostics). Overhead is a session-level figure and is never spread over agents or turns. For day rollups, spread each window's overhead over days in proportion to that window's covered attributed cost, so day totals add up to best cost. If two sessions carry a window with the same From, it counts once, for the session with the earlier startedAt.
- CLI / doctor (3.3): show per session best, reported (windows), attributed, overhead, uncovered, inherited; cost tables state how much of the total is reported vs attributed; doctor prints the covered/reported ratio overall and its distribution, and lists sessions with uncovered spend.
- Validation (3.5): expected on the real corpus — 74 interactive sessions with windows, reported $2,682.89, covered attributed $2,484.99 (ratio 0.926; per session median 0.934, p10 0.861, max below 1.0), uncovered $145 ($113 before first window, $30 between windows, $2 after last). A covered ratio above 1.0 in any session means a bug or a wrong price: investigate it.

title: Explorer 3.1: reconciler, work queue and `explorer scan`
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: internal/engine — the loop that makes stored digests match the transcripts — and the `explorer scan` subcommand. PLAN.md §3, §4 "Other harnesses later" and §6.

Harness interface first
- Define internal/harness: the small interface the engine drives — Name(); Discover() returning session sources (key, project key, fingerprint); Build(source) returning a model.SessionDigest. Leave room for the two things the serve bead adds (naming live sessions, mapping a hook event to a session) but do not design beyond what one implementation needs. No registry, no plugins: main passes the engine a list of adapters.
- Implement it for Claude in internal/claude (a thin adapter over internal/claude/discover and internal/claude/digest). The engine, and everything outside internal/claude, must not import the Claude subpackages directly.

Engine
- Reconcile(): for each harness, discover sources; read stored digest headers; a session needs work when it has no digest, its fingerprint differs, or schema/parser version differs. A stored digest whose source no longer exists is marked sourceMissing (once) and kept.
- Work queue: in memory only, keyed by session so a session is queued at most once and never processed by two workers at the same time; a session changed while being processed is processed again afterwards. Priority lane for sessions flagged live.
- Worker pool (default GOMAXPROCS, configurable): BuildSession → store write. A panic or error in one session is recovered, logged, and stored as an error stub with the fingerprint so it is retried only when the files change.
- Callback/event hook after each write (session id, digest) so the catalog and server can subscribe later.
- Progress reporting for long scans (counts, bytes, rate) via a callback; `explorer scan` prints it and a final summary: sessions seen, processed, unchanged, failed, missing, elapsed.
- There is no persisted queue or journal. Correctness after a crash comes from reconciling again.

Out of scope: timers, hooks, live following, the lock (serve bead); catalog.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=testdata copy and a temp EXPLORER_HOME: first scan writes a digest per session; second scan processes nothing; appending to a transcript reprocesses only that session; deleting a transcript marks sourceMissing and keeps the digest; a parser-version bump reprocesses all; a session that makes the builder fail yields an error stub and is not retried until its file changes; simulated crash (digest half-written as a temp file, or some digests missing) converges on the next scan. Queue test: the same session enqueued many times concurrently is never processed in parallel (run with -race). A test drives the engine with a fake second harness and shows its digests land under <EXPLORER_HOME>/<that name>/ without the engine knowing anything about it; a check (test or go list) shows internal/engine does not import internal/claude/discover, digest or transcript. make test and make vet pass.
close_reason: Harness interface, claude adapter, engine (reconciler, in-memory queue, workers, callbacks) and explorer scan done; tests cover all acceptance criteria, race-clean.

title: Explorer 2.2: Assemble — agents, topology and cost rollup
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: internal/claude/digest gains Assemble: main-file result (may be absent for orphans) + agent-file results + agent metas → the agents[] part of model.SessionDigest and the per-turn agent fields. PLAN.md §5 (Agent); transcript-format.md §5.

- One model.Agent per agent file. kind: teammate (meta teamName or taskKind in_process_teammate), fork (meta isFork or agentType "fork"), compact (id starts with "acompact"), else subagent.
- Linkage ladder, first match wins, recorded in Agent.linkage:
  1. meta — meta.toolUseId equals an Agent tool_use id seen in the main file or any agent file.
  2. tool-result — an agent-spawn tool_result whose toolUseResult.agentId equals this agent id; use its tool_use_id.
  3. name — teammates: meta.name equals the input.name of an Agent tool_use; take the earliest not already claimed.
  4. prompt — the agent's first prompt text equals the input.prompt of an unclaimed Agent tool_use.
  5. unresolved — parent is the session root; count in diagnostics.unresolvedAgents.
- parentAgentId: the agent whose file contains the spawning tool_use (null when it is the main file). meta.parentAgentId is used when no tool_use was found. depth from meta.spawnDepth when present, else computed from the parent chain. Guard against cycles.
- spawnToolUseId, spawnTurn (main-file turn index of the spawning tool_use; for nested agents, the spawn turn of the top-level ancestor), background (run_in_background input or async_launched result), description / agentType / model / name from meta, falling back to the tool_use input and to the model actually seen in the agent's messages.
- status: completed if a tool_result with status completed exists for the spawn, or a task-notification for this agent id reports completed; killed if an agents_killed event follows its last activity and nothing completed it, or a notification reports killed/failed; otherwise open.
- prompt = first prompt of the agent file; finalText = final text of its last turn; inbox = later prompts (at, from when the origin identifies a sender, text).
- cost = the agent's own messages; subtreeUSD = own + all descendants. Each main-file turn gets spawned[] and costWithAgents = its own cost + subtreeUSD of agents spawned in it.
- Message ids shared between agent files of the same session (forks): each is counted once, owned by the agent with the earliest first timestamp, then the smaller id. model.Message.agentId records the owner.
- Session cost = main messages + all agent messages, each message id once.
- compactions per agent.
- Orphan sessions (no main result): agents attach to the root, unresolved.

Out of scope: session-level descriptive fields; cross-session de-duplication (catalog).
acceptance_criteria: Tests over the fixtures: every rung of the linkage ladder is exercised and asserted; nested agent has the right parent, depth and spawnTurn; teammate has kind teammate and its later message in inbox; fork siblings do not double count shared message ids; subtreeUSD and costWithAgents equal hand-computed values; statuses completed / open / killed each asserted; orphan session yields agents with total cost. make test and make vet pass.

title: Explorer 2.1: digest Builder — turns, messages, cost, compaction for one file
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: internal/claude/digest gains Builder, a reducer over the records of ONE transcript file (a main file or an agent file). PLAN.md §5 including "Turn rules" and "Compaction"; transcript-format.md §3, §4, §6.

Shape
- NewBuilder(pricer), Apply(record) for each record in file order, Result() returning an intermediate per-file result. It must be a reducer: Apply never needs records that come later, so the engine can feed appended records to a kept Builder. Result() may be called repeatedly and finalises a copy.
- The per-file result holds everything Assemble (next bead) needs: messages, turns, compactions, every Agent tool_use seen (tool_use id, input name / description / prompt / subagent_type / model / run_in_background, the turn index and message it occurred in, timestamp), every agent-spawn tool_result (tool_use_id + toolUseResult status, agentId or name), task-notification prompts with their task id and status, agents_killed events, metadata records (titles, agent-name, last-prompt, cost-state list, away summaries, cwd / branch / version / entrypoint / sessionKind sets), first and last timestamps, counters and diagnostics.

Messages
- Group assistant lines by message.id; usage comes from the LAST line of the group; count once. Skip model "<synthetic>" for cost. Unknown models go to diagnostics.unpricedModels.
- Each billed message becomes a model.Message with timestamp, model, token breakdown, usd, and the turn index it falls in.
- Text for a message = its text blocks concatenated in order across its lines.

Turns (main-file semantics; an agent file uses the same segmentation so its first prompt and later inbox messages fall out naturally)
- A turn starts at a prompt record (transcript.IsPrompt). Origin via the classification helpers.
- A bare interruption marker flags the previous turn interrupted and starts no turn; marker + text starts a turn with the marker stripped.
- userText is the whole prompt text (text blocks joined); count image blocks in images. uuid is the prompt record's uuid.
- finalText: the text of the last assistant message in the turn that has any text; if shorter than 80 characters and an earlier text message exists in the turn, prepend that one with a blank line between.
- Per turn: startedAt, endedAt (last record of the turn), durationMs (turn_duration record if present, else endedAt-startedAt), assistantMessages, toolCalls, toolsByName, filesTouched (file_path of Edit / Write / NotebookEdit tool inputs, unique, in order), cost, contextTokens (input + cache read + cache creation of the last billed message), epoch.
- Assistant activity before the first prompt (orphan agent files, resumed files) goes into a turn 0 with origin "continuation" and empty userText rather than being dropped — its cost must not be lost.

Record identity
- Skip any record whose uuid was already seen in this file (first occurrence wins). Records are ordered by file position; never follow parentUuid or logicalParentUuid to order or to find things.

Compaction (append-only: the file keeps the whole history; see transcript-format.md §6)
- compact_boundary starts a new epoch. Record at, trigger, preTokens, postTokens, durationMs and the whole text of the isCompactSummary record that follows (usually the next record, sometimes one later; may be missing). The summary record is not a prompt and starts no turn.
- Turns before the boundary are kept and counted as usual. The turn index recorded on the Compaction is the last turn before it (or -1).
- A file that begins with a boundary yields a Compaction at epoch start with no earlier turns.
- A compaction in the middle of a turn does not split the turn; the turn's epoch is the epoch at its start.

Abandoned branches (PLAN.md §5 "Branching and forking"; transcript-format.md §9)
- Keep a uuid → parent map over ALL records that have a uuid (attachments are part of the chain), using parentUuid, or logicalParentUuid on a compact boundary.
- In Result(): the active path is the set of ancestors of the last user/assistant record in the file. If the walk reaches a parent that is not in the file, stop and treat every record positioned before the last record reached as active — a broken chain must never mark history as abandoned.
- A turn is abandoned when its prompt record is not on the active path and it is positioned after the earliest active record. Turns stay in file order and their cost still counts. Parallel tool results are not branches and must not cause any turn to be flagged.
- This is a finalisation step, so it does not break the reducer property.

Determinism: no wall clock, no map-order dependence.

Out of scope: agents, linking, session-level fields, golden digests of whole sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests over the fixtures: multi-line message counted once with last usage; expected turn counts, origins, userText and finalText for plain, slash-command, interruption and compaction scenarios; hand-computed cost matches per turn and in total; compaction epochs and whole summaries captured, turns on both sides of a boundary present, the file-begins-with-boundary case, the dangling logicalParentUuid case and the repeated-uuid case each asserted; in the rewind fixture exactly the abandoned turns are flagged, the replaced-prompt turn is flagged, the parallel-tool-call shape flags nothing, and a file with a dangling parent flags nothing before the break; hostile-input file processes without error and reports bad lines and unknown types; feeding a file in two halves to one Builder gives the same Result as feeding it whole. make test and make vet pass.

title: Explorer 0.2: digest schema and transcript record types (the contract)
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: the two shared type packages everything else builds on. This is the contract; it gets reviewed before other work starts, so favour clarity over cleverness.

internal/model — the digest schema of PLAN.md §5, as Go structs with JSON tags
- SessionDigest, Cost, ModelCost, Turn, Agent, Compaction, Message, Recap, Lineage, Stats, Reported, Diagnostics, SourceFile.
- This package is harness-neutral: nothing in it may be specific to Claude Code. SessionDigest carries harness ("claude" today; codex, pi later), project (the directory path the session started in — the project's identity across harnesses) next to projectKey (the harness's storage key), and harnessVersions. A session is identified by (harness, id); provide a SessionKey type for that.
- Turn carries uuid (the prompt record's uuid, used to match copied turns across sessions) and abandoned (on a branch the session rewound away from) — see PLAN.md §5 "Branching and forking".
- Enumerations as typed strings with constants: session kind, turn origin, agent kind, agent status (completed | killed | open), linkage, end state, compaction trigger.
- SchemaVersion constant. Helpers on Cost: Add(other), and a method to add one priced message.
- Follow the JSON conventions in CLAUDE.md. Texts are whole strings, never truncated.
- Write explorer/docs/digest-schema.md describing every field in one line each (hand-written or generated — it must match the structs).

internal/claude/transcript — tolerant structs for the records in docs/transcript-format.md
- An envelope struct with the fields of §2 (including parentUuid and, on compact boundaries, logicalParentUuid — the branch logic needs them), and typed accessors/structs for: assistant message (id, model, content blocks, stop_reason, usage incl. cache_creation breakdown, speed, server_tool_use), user message (string-or-array content), tool_use and tool_result blocks, envelope toolUseResult for agent spawns (completed / async_launched / teammate_spawned), compact_boundary metadata, cost-state, ai-title / custom-title / agent-name / last-prompt, away_summary, turn_duration, origin / promptSource, forkedFrom, agent meta.json.
- message.content for user records is a string OR an array — handle both.
- Classification helpers that need no state: IsPrompt (user record that is not a tool result, not isMeta, not isCompactSummary), prompt origin from origin.kind / promptSource with the text-prefix fallback of §4, interruption-marker detection, slash-command extraction.
- Decode must never fail on unknown fields or unknown record types; an unknown type yields a record whose Type is set and nothing else.

Out of scope: reading files, pricing, building digests.

description:

comments.author: Zsolt Terek
comments.text:
Prototype built, not committed. Files: explorer/web/src/features/spend/{model.ts,model.test.ts,SpendGraph.tsx,TurnInspector.tsx,DevSpend.tsx}, plus one route in App.tsx (/dev/spend/:harness/:id). `make web-check` passes (180 tests, 16 new).

What it is
- One graph, one turn axis, three tracks: spend (running total or per turn; split by who or by token class), agent lanes, context with compactions.
- Agent spend is placed by message time on the turn that was running, not on the spawn turn. On the spawn turn a long-lived teammate produced a false cliff of $150.
- Agent lanes: one row per agent from spawn to last activity, rows shared by agents that do not overlap, a connector to the parent's row, cells darker where it spent more, name after the row where it fits.
- Cache miss: a message that writes again at least half of what the same agent's previous message (same model) left cached, 5k tokens minimum. Own series in both splits, a bar on the context track for the main agent, the gap since the previous message, and what a cache read would have cost.
- Per-class dollars: the web has no price table, so the two prices per model (input, cache read) are fitted to the messages by least squares. On three real sessions the fit returned the price table exactly, and both splits add up to the digest total to the cent.
- Click pins a turn: prompt, reply, dollars and tokens by class, each cache miss in words, agents at work in that turn, agent detail.

Checked on real history (read-only, scratch home, no hooks): five sessions between 52 and 164 turns, light and dark.

Known gaps
- The mock (`dev/gen.ts` messagesOf) emits main-agent messages without cache writes, so on the mock the graph shows the main agent only. The mock needs agent messages and a few cache misses before workers can build on this.
- More than half of the misses come seconds after the previous message, so the cache had not expired. Cause not established (compaction, a model switch, a changed prompt prefix). The Go side can see more than the web can.
- For the real version the digest should carry dollars per token class per message and mark cache misses, so that the web stops fitting prices (additive schema change).
- Not done: zoom on a turn range, more than 18 lanes (folded into the last row), the series palette in dark fails the validator's lightness band (existing tokens, colour-blind separation passes).
- Sessions forked into another session get a diamond on the axis; turns copied from a parent are shaded and left out of the total. Neither was exercised on a real fork with inherited turns.

comments.author: Zsolt Terek
comments.text:
Second version, after the user's feedback on the first (same files, still uncommitted; `make web-check` passes, 182 tests).

Feedback: the running total is not useful (it always integrates), and spreading agent spend over the main turns mixes two things. The question is "which of my decisions had a huge cost impact". An agent run is atomic: the orchestrator decided, picked a model, and that cost something. It matters where it branches off (the decision) and where its result arrives (it may shape the decisions there).

What the model is now (`model.ts`)
- Step: one turn of the main session, main agent only (compaction calls on their turn).
- Unit: one piece of work handed to an agent the main session launched, with its own sub-agents inside. A sub-agent or fork is one unit. A teammate is one unit per message it was sent (`inbox`), from that message to its last billed message before the next one; a message that started no work is not a unit. On the largest real session a $156 teammate becomes 23 units of $0.10 to $35.
- Launch turn: the spawn turn, or the turn running when the message was sent. Return turn: the last `peer` turn in the unit's window that names the teammate (`teammate_id`), else the turn running at its last message, plus one when a background agent is followed by a task notification. These are heuristics in the web; the digest should carry both turns.
- Decision: a turn a person typed (origin human or command) with every step and every unit launched until the next one.
- Totals equal the digest's attributed cost to the cent on five real sessions.

What the graph is now (`SpendGraph.tsx`)
- Context of the main session on top (compactions, a bar per main-agent cache miss).
- The main line: a dot per typed prompt, a bracket with the decision's total above it.
- Above the line a bar per turn (main agent). Below it a bar per unit under its launch turn, as tall as it cost, with a tail to the turn its report came in and a dashed riser back to the line. One dollar scale for all bars.
- Rows: one per launched agent, shared by agents that do not overlap.
- Under the graph: the decisions ranked by cost; a pinned turn shows prompt, reply, what the main agent paid for, units launched there, reports that came in there; a selected unit shows what it was asked, what it paid for, its cache misses, its sub-agents, then the agent.

Open
- One scale for steps and units keeps them comparable, but where agent work dominates the steps are a few pixels tall.
- A prompt typed while agents are still working takes over their later reports (they are counted under the newer decision).
- Nested agents are inside their unit and not drawn.
- Mock data still lacks agent messages and inbox messages.

title: Explorer: ship the Explorer binary from the release workflow and install.sh, in place of the old Merlin binary
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md, explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/Makefile, and the two files this bead rewrites: .github/workflows/release.yml and install.sh (both at the repository root, both written for the old Bun/TS Merlin).

Goal: the GitHub release built by CI ships the Explorer binary instead of the old Merlin binary, and `install.sh` installs it. The old Merlin sources stay in the repository for reference only: nothing builds or ships them any more.

## Decide before starting (ask the user)

1. **Name.** What is the installed command and the release asset called: `explorer` (assets `explorer-<os>-<arch>`, state under `~/.explorer`) or `merlin` (assets `merlin-<os>-<arch>`)? Explorer has not been renamed, so this bead assumes `explorer` unless told otherwise. It matters for people who have the old binary: its `merlin upgrade` downloads `merlin-<os>-<arch>` from the latest release, so keeping the asset name would silently replace their program with a different one, and changing it makes their upgrade fail with a 404. Neither is harmful if nobody but the user has it installed; say which is intended.
2. **Version.** The old binary's last tag is v0.1.1. Does Explorer continue that sequence (v0.2.0) or start its own?
3. **Where install.sh is served from.** The README says `curl -fsSL https://merlin.dev/install.sh | bash`; the workflow also uploads install.sh as a release asset. Find out what serves merlin.dev/install.sh and whether it needs a change.

## Release workflow

Replace the Bun build with the Go build; keep the shape (tag `v*` or manual run, a macOS job that signs and notarizes, a Linux job, a release job with SHA256SUMS).

- Build the web UI once (`make web`: bun, version pinned as today) and embed it: `go build -tags embedui -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=<version>" ./cmd/explorer`, from explorer/. Go version from explorer/go.mod (`actions/setup-go` with `go-version-file`).
- Targets: darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, all with `CGO_ENABLED=0`. Checked on 2026-10-02: these four cross-compile cleanly. A static Go binary runs on musl systems too, so the separate `-musl` assets go away. Windows does not compile (`internal/daemon` uses flock) and is dropped; note it in the README.
- Keep the asset arch names `x64` / `arm64` so install.sh's detection stays as it is (Go calls x64 `amd64`).
- macOS: keep Developer ID signing and notarization with the existing secrets. The entitlements file (build/entitlements.mac.plist) exists for Bun's JIT; a Go binary needs none, so sign with the hardened runtime and no entitlements, and verify the signed binary still runs (`explorer version`) on the runner.
- Run the checks before building: `make test`, `make vet`, `make web-check`. A release must not be cut from a tree that fails them.
- Smoke test each natively runnable artifact in CI: `explorer version` prints the release version, and `explorer serve --no-hooks` against the fixtures (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=explorer/testdata/claude`, a temp `EXPLORER_HOME`) answers `GET /` with the UI (not the "UI was not built" page) and `GET /api/sessions` with JSON.
- Add a second, small workflow that runs the same checks on pushes and pull requests, so failures show up before a tag does.

## install.sh

- Download `<name>-<os>-<arch>`, verify against SHA256SUMS, install to the same locations as today. Remove the musl detection. Rename the knobs to match the name decided above and keep the old `MERLIN_*` spellings working if the name stays `merlin`.
- There is no `setup` subcommand: Explorer installs its Claude Code hooks when `explorer serve` starts (and `--no-hooks` skips that). After installing, do not start anything and do not touch `~/.claude`; print what to run next (`explorer serve`, then the URL of the UI) and that the first start adds five hook entries to `~/.claude/settings.json` with a backup.
- If an old Merlin binary is found on PATH, say so and leave it alone.
- Must stay safe under `curl | bash`: `set -euo pipefail`, everything inside functions or otherwise robust to a truncated download, no prompts.

## Not in this bead

A self-update command, a launchd/systemd unit to keep the daemon running (PLAN.md M6), Homebrew, and renaming Explorer to Merlin (`~/.merlin`).

## Docs

Rewrite the install and upgrade sections of the root README for Explorer (upgrade = run the installer again), and say at the top of the README that the TypeScript sources are the earlier Merlin, kept for reference. Add a short "Releasing" section to explorer/CLAUDE.md or PLAN.md: how to cut a release and which secrets it needs.
acceptance_criteria: The three questions were answered by the user and the answers are recorded on the bead; a manual run of the release workflow on a test version produces the four signed (macOS: notarized) binaries, SHA256SUMS and install.sh, with no old Merlin binary among the assets; each binary reports the release version and serves the embedded UI; the checks workflow runs on push; install.sh, run with a pinned version and a temp install dir on macOS and in a Linux container (glibc and Alpine), installs a working binary, verifies the checksum, starts nothing and leaves ~/.claude untouched; README and the release notes are updated; the old Merlin sources are unchanged.

title: Explorer 5.5: Agents card and context chart
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules, the "Web UI" section), explorer/docs/ui.md (all of it; you build the Agents card and the Context chart of section 9), explorer/docs/digest-schema.md (Agent, Turn, Compaction), explorer/docs/api.md, and the closing note of merlin-t8s.18.1.

Goal: make the subagent topology of a session and its cost readable at a glance, and show how the context grew and was compacted.

You own: explorer/web/src/features/agents/** and explorer/web/src/features/context/** only. The component signatures were fixed by the scaffold (`AgentsCard`, `ContextChart`); the Session page, built by another worker at the same time, mounts them and owns the selection state. Do not change the signatures and do not edit features/session. To look at your work in place, use the session page as it is (stub or not); a dev-only route under /dev that mounts your two components over a session id is fine too and stays in your directories. `src/api`, `src/lib` and `src/ui` are shared: additive changes only, named in your closing note.

Ports for this bead: fixture daemon 7445, Vite 5185, mock API 7455.

## Agents card

- The tree comes from `digest.agents[]` through `parentAgentId` (null: spawned by the main agent). Use or extend `buildAgentTree` in src/lib; orphans (a parent id not in the list) hang under the root with a mark, a cycle must not hang the page.
- A node: kind (subagent, teammate, fork), type or name, description (one line, clamped), model label, status, background mark, own cost, subtree cost, and a bar of the subtree cost against the session's attributed total. Children are ordered by start time. Subtrees deeper than three levels start collapsed; a session with 100 agents must stay readable (group consecutive siblings of the same type under one expandable line when there are more than eight, with their summed cost).
- Head of the card: number of agents, the attributed cost of all agents versus the main agent, and the deepest level.
- `linkage: unresolved` agents are listed apart, under "not tied to a spawn". `kind: compact` entries are listed last, quietly, with their cost: they are compaction calls, not topology.
- Selecting a node (also by `selectedAgentId` from outside) opens the agent detail under the tree: prompt (`PlainText`, clamped), final text (`Prose`, clamped), inbox messages, started / ended / duration, assistant messages, tool calls with tools by name, its compactions, cost by model, and "spawned in turn N" calling `onSelectTurn`. A selected node deep in a collapsed subtree expands its ancestors and scrolls into view.
- All agent figures are attributed from tokens; say so once in the card. Output tokens of agents can be undercounted in transcripts, so the card's footnote reads: "agent cost is recomputed from token counts and is a lower bound".

## Context chart

- An SVG sawtooth of `turn.contextTokens` over turn index (turns without a value are skipped, not drawn as zero), with a vertical marker at each compaction showing pre → post. The y axis is labelled in tokens (`200k`), the x axis in turn indexes.
- Hover shows turn index, context size and the first line of the prompt; click calls `onSelectTurn`. Keyboard: the chart is focusable and left / right move the cursor, Enter selects.
- Abandoned turns are drawn faint. Hidden when fewer than 3 turns have a value. It must stay legible at 380px wide with 600 turns.

title: Explorer 5.2: API additions for the UI
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/docs/api.md, explorer/docs/ui.md (sections 6, 8 and 10 say what the UI needs these for).

Goal: the few things the web UI needs that the API does not give yet. All additive; no digest change, so ParserVersion and SchemaVersion stay as they are.

You own: explorer/internal/server/**, explorer/docs/api.md, additive changes in explorer/internal/catalog/**, and for the last item explorer/cmd/explorer/cmd_doctor.go. Another worker is creating explorer/web and explorer/internal/webui and editing the Makefile and cmd_serve.go at the same time: do not edit those. This bead also covers merlin-t8s.21; close both.

## 1. Session summary additions

`SessionSummary` (list rows, the session-updated event, the head of the detail) gains:

- `humanTurns` (int): the digest's stats.humanTurns.
- `lastPrompt` `{turn, at, text, truncated}`, omitted when the session has no human turn: the last turn with origin `human` that is not abandoned; when every human turn is abandoned, the last human turn. `text` is a preview: runs of whitespace collapsed to one space, trimmed, cut to 300 runes at a rune boundary; `truncated` says it was cut.
- `recap` `{at, text, truncated}`, omitted when the session has none: the last recap, same preview rule.

The preview is the one place the API shortens a text; say so in docs/api.md, and that the whole text is in the detail's digest. Stored digests are not touched.

## 2. Cost split

`GET /api/cost` accepts `split=project|model|kind`. It must differ from `by` and is refused (400) with `by=session`, with an unknown value, or when equal to `by`. Every row then carries `split: [{key, totalUSD, reportedUSD, attributedUSD}]`, largest first, ties by key. The parts of a row add up to the row (test this for every `by`/`split` pair on the fixtures, to within 1e-9), and the `(overhead)` model row appears as a part where it applies. Without `split` the response is unchanged, byte for byte (the existing snapshot tests must pass unedited).

## 3. session-state event

`/api/events` emits `session-state` with data `{"key": {...}, "state": "idle", "previous": "busy"}` when a listable session (not scripted) changes between busy, idle, recent and ended. Liveness comes from the registry and the clock already in `Options`; look at it on an interval (`Options.StateInterval`, default 2 s). No event for the first look after a stream opens. The stream must still never hold up the indexer, and a `session-updated` for the same session in the same tick is enough on its own (it carries the state): do not send both. Tests with a fake registry and clock: busy to idle, idle to ended, recent to ended by time alone, a new session appearing, and no duplicate events across two streams.

## 4. doctor (from merlin-t8s.21)

In `explorer doctor`, the table of sessions whose transcripts add up to more than was reported lists rows with a gap of -$0.0000 (float noise). Show a row only when the gap is below -$0.005. Update the snapshot test.

## Docs

Update docs/api.md for all of the above, with examples from the fixtures.

## Checking against the real history

As in the earlier beads: read-only, with a scratch `EXPLORER_HOME`, and `serve` only with `--no-hooks`, on port 7442. Report counts and timings only (how many sessions have a lastPrompt, a recap; response sizes and times of /api/sessions and /api/cost with split); never prompt text, titles or paths.
acceptance_criteria: The three summary fields are served in /api/sessions, the detail and session-updated, with tests for the abandoned-turn rule, the 300-rune cut on multi-byte text and whitespace collapsing; split works for every valid by/split pair with the sum identity tested, is refused where specified, and leaves split-less responses byte-identical; session-state is emitted per the rules with the listed tests; doctor shows no -$0.0000 rows; docs/api.md is updated; make test and make vet pass; verified read-only against the real history with a scratch EXPLORER_HOME (counts and timings only in the closing note, no transcript text).

comments.text:
COST DESIGN CHANGE (lead, after checking the real corpus) — supersedes anything in this bead that says "reported = the last cost-state record" or "best cost = reported if present else attributed".

Fact: a cost-state record is a running total for one PROCESS RUN that began at its startTime. A session therefore has one reported WINDOW per distinct startTime: from startTime to the timestamp of the last record before that window's last cost-state. Spending outside every window (before the first, between two, after the last write) is not reported at all. Inside windows the transcript-derived cost is always <= reported (about 7% under). See explorer/docs/transcript-format.md section 8 and PLAN.md sections 3 (principle 6), 5 and 7.

Schema: model.Reported now has Windows []ReportedWindow{From, To, TotalUSD, ByModel}; Reported.TotalUSD and ByModel are the sums over windows. See explorer/docs/digest-schema.md.

Rules:
- Building the digest (2.3): group cost-state records by startTime in file order. For each group: From = startTime (epoch milliseconds); To = timestamp of the last transcript record that precedes the group's LAST cost-state record in the file; TotalUSD and ByModel from that last record (model names normalised, "[1m]" stripped). If a total decreases while startTime is unchanged, start a new window there. Windows are ordered by From. The Builder's CostStateRecord needs the timestamp of the preceding record: add it additively (field At) if it is not there. linesAdded / linesRemoved in stats = sums over windows' last records.
- Catalog (3.2): a message is "covered" when its timestamp lies within a window of its session (allow 1 second of slack at both ends). bestCost(session) = Reported.TotalUSD + attributed cost of the session's OWNED messages that are not covered. Flag: exact (has windows, nothing owned is uncovered), partial (has windows and uncovered owned spend), estimated (no windows). overhead(session) = Reported.TotalUSD - attributed cost of covered messages (never negative in practice; clamp at 0 and count clamps in diagnostics). Overhead is a session-level figure and is never spread over agents or turns. For day rollups, spread each window's overhead over days in proportion to that window's covered attributed cost, so day totals add up to best cost. If two sessions carry a window with the same From, it counts once, for the session with the earlier startedAt.
- CLI / doctor (3.3): show per session best, reported (windows), attributed, overhead, uncovered, inherited; cost tables state how much of the total is reported vs attributed; doctor prints the covered/reported ratio overall and its distribution, and lists sessions with uncovered spend.
- Validation (3.5): expected on the real corpus — 74 interactive sessions with windows, reported $2,682.89, covered attributed $2,484.99 (ratio 0.926; per session median 0.934, p10 0.861, max below 1.0), uncovered $145 ($113 before first window, $30 between windows, $2 after last). A covered ratio above 1.0 in any session means a bug or a wrong price: investigate it.

Every session whose whole-session ratio exceeded 1.0 is explained by spend outside windows. So there is no evidence of an overpriced table entry — but the "assumed" cache-read prices (fable-5, opus-4-x, sonnet-4-6, sonnet-5-5) have NO verification either way, because no reported window contains those models except where noted; check which assumed models do appear inside windows and solve for their implied rates.
- Agent linkage: 286 teammates by name, 122 by meta, 9 by tool-result, 82 unresolved (56 subagents + 26 compact agents, all from CC <= 2.1.71 with no meta and usually no parent transcript). Status: 485 completed, 9 open, 5 killed.
- Copied sessions and cost-state: all nine copied pairs predate cost-state, so whether a copy carries its parent's cost-state records is still unanswerable from this corpus. Say so.

Compare, per model, transcript token totals against cost-state modelUsage (input, output, cache read, cache creation) for the sessions with the largest overhead. Test the hypotheses: (a) final lines with stop_reason null carry a partial output_tokens count; (b) the compaction call (does overhead grow with number of compactions x preTokens?); (c) recaps (away_summary count), titles, agent progress summaries — the always-present haiku line in cost-state with no haiku message in the transcript is one visible piece: how much of the overhead is haiku? (d) subagent vs main: is the shortfall concentrated in the subagents' model? Quantify each as a share of the $204 overhead where you can; say plainly what remains unexplained.
2. Verify or correct the assumed prices where the data allows.
3. Abandoned turns: count per session, confirm none is large.
4. doctor polish: the format-drift table currently prints one row per Claude Code version even when every row is clean (95 rows on this corpus). Print only versions with bad lines or unknown types, plus one summary line ("95 versions, no bad lines, no unknown record types"); keep the full table behind a flag. Update its snapshots.
5. Since output changed several times during review without a version bump, set digest.ParserVersion to 2 as your last code change, so any store written by an earlier build is rebuilt.

Method: build with make build; run with EXPLORER_HOME set to a scratch directory under your temp dir (NOT ~/.explorer) and the real ~/.claude as source (read-only: never write there, and do not run `explorer serve` without --no-hooks, and not `explorer hooks install`). description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: the long-running process. PLAN.md §6.

description:

title: Explorer 2.3: session-level fields and golden digests
description:

Goal: finish internal/claude/digest: a function that takes a discovered session source and returns the complete model.SessionDigest, plus golden files for every fixture. PLAN.md §5.

- BuildSession(source, pricer): reads the files (transcript reader), runs Builder per file, Assemble, then fills the session fields.
- source = the fingerprint list; parserVersion = a constant in this package that is bumped whenever output would change; schemaVersion from model.
- harness = "claude"; id, projectKey; project = cwd = first cwd seen (the directory the session started in); cwds / gitBranches / harnessVersions = all seen in order of first appearance.

- reported: the LAST cost-state record — totalUSD and per-model tokens and usd, model names normalised; linesAdded / linesRemoved into stats.

- Golden tests: testdata/golden/<scenario>.json for every fixture session, with a -update flag to regenerate. Review each golden file by hand against testdata/README.md before committing it — the golden files are the specification, not just a snapshot.

title: Explorer 1.3: session discovery and fingerprints
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: internal/claude/discover walks the Claude projects tree and returns every session with the files that belong to it. See transcript-format.md §1.

- Input: the projects directory. Output: a list of session sources: project key (top-level directory name), session id, main transcript path (may be absent), agent files (jsonl + optional meta path, agent id parsed from the file name), and a fingerprint = sorted list of (path, size, mtimeNs) over all of those files.
- A main transcript is a *.jsonl whose basename is a UUID and which is not under a subagents directory. Anything else (other jsonl files, tool-results, memory, custom-title.json, sessions-index.json) is ignored.
- Orphans: a <uuid>/subagents directory with agent files but no <uuid>.jsonl still yields a session source.
- Walk recursively: a project directory can contain another project directory. The project key is always the top-level directory.
- Unreadable directories and files are skipped and reported, not fatal.
- Fingerprints compare equal iff the same files have the same size and mtime. Provide Equal and a stable string form.
- Must be cheap: stat only, no file contents.

Out of scope: reading transcripts; deciding what is stale (that is the engine).

title: Explorer 1.1: transcript line reader
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: internal/claude/transcript gains the file reader.

- Read a .jsonl file as a stream of records. Lines can exceed 1 MB: use bufio.Reader.ReadBytes or an equivalently unbounded approach, not bufio.Scanner defaults.
- Only lines terminated by \n are consumed. A trailing partial line is left unread and the reported offset stops before it.
- Each record is delivered with its decoded envelope and its raw bytes. A line that is not valid JSON increments a bad-line counter and is skipped.
- Resume support: the reader reports the byte offset after the last consumed line and a guard (hash of up to the last 256 bytes before that offset). OpenAt(path, offset, guard) resumes only if the guard still matches; otherwise it reports that a full re-read is needed. A file shorter than the offset also means full re-read.
- Reader for agent meta.json (missing file is not an error).

Out of scope: interpreting records.
acceptance_criteria: Tests using the hostile-input fixtures: >1 MB line read intact; corrupt line counted and skipped; partial last line not consumed and consumed after it is completed; resume from offset yields only new records; rewritten file (same size, changed content before the offset) is detected via the guard. make test and make vet pass.

title: Explorer 0.3: synthetic transcript fixtures
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: a hand-written fixture tree that every later bead tests against. Real transcripts must never be copied — invent short, obviously fake content ("add a login page", "done, 3 files changed").

Layout: explorer/testdata/claude/projects/<project-key>/... mirroring the real layout in transcript-format.md §1, so the directory can be used directly as CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=testdata/claude.

One session (or pair) per scenario, each small (5–40 lines), with record shapes exactly as documented:
1. plain: two human turns, tool use, end_turn, ai-title, turn_duration.
2. multi-line-message: one API message split across 3 lines with the same message.id and usage that differs between lines (last is final).
3. slash-command and local-command output; a custom-title overriding the ai-title.
4. interruption: bare "[Request interrupted by user]", and one followed by new text.
5. compaction: two compact_boundary + isCompactSummary pairs, one auto and one manual, one without postTokens, one whose logicalParentUuid names a uuid that is not in the file, with turns before, between and after. Plus: a file that BEGINS with a boundary + summary; a file containing a record whose uuid repeats an earlier record (must be skipped); a subagent file that compacts.
6. sync subagent: Agent tool_use, agent file + meta.json with toolUseId, tool_result with toolUseResult status completed.
7. background subagent: async_launched, later a <task-notification> prompt for its task id.
8. nested subagent: a subagent that spawns another (meta parentAgentId, spawnDepth 2).
9. teammate: Agent tool_use with name, teammate_spawned result, agent-a<name>-<hex> file, meta with teamName, a later message delivered to it.
10. fork agent: meta isFork, sharing some message ids with a sibling agent file.
11. linkage fallbacks: one agent linkable only by toolUseResult.agentId, one only by prompt text, one not linkable at all.
12. orphan: a <uuid>/subagents directory with agent files and no <uuid>.jsonl.
13. copied history (transcript-format.md §9), each a pair where session B starts with a verbatim copy of session A's records (same uuid, message.id, timestamp; sessionId rewritten to B):
    a. continuation, unmarked: A stops at the copy point, B carries on.
    b. fork, unmarked: A has further turns of its own after the copy point, and so does B.
    c. fork marked with forkedFrom on every copied record.
    d. partial copy marked by session_id != sessionId: B begins with a compact boundary + summary and only the tail of A.
    e. picked up by an SDK client: A is all entrypoint cli; B's copied records are cli and its own records are sdk-cli (B must NOT be classified as scripted).
19. rewind inside one file: a prompt with a response, then a second prompt whose parentUuid is the same as the first prompt's (the first branch is abandoned); also a prompt replaced before any response; also a parallel-tool-call shape (one assistant line with two tool results as children) that must NOT count as a branch. Include attachment records in the parentUuid chain, as real files do.
14. sdk one-shot: entrypoint sdk-cli, one prompt, cost-state at the end.
15. cost-state: an interactive session with two cost-state records (cumulative) and several models, including one with a [1m] suffix and a subagent on a different model.
16. hostile input: a line over 1 MB, a corrupt line in the middle, an unknown record type, a file ending in a partial line, an assistant record with model "<synthetic>".
17. cwd change: worktree-state / relocated, gitBranch change.
18. day boundary: a session whose messages straddle local midnight (document the timezone the test must set).
Also: a non-transcript jsonl in a project dir (must be ignored), a nested project directory, and a fake sessions/<pid>.json.

Token counts should be small round numbers so expected costs can be computed by hand. Put the hand-computed expected cost for each priced scenario in the README.

Write explorer/testdata/README.md: one line per scenario saying what it exercises and the expected headline facts (turn count, agent count, total cost).

A small generator script is acceptable for the >1 MB line only; everything else is committed as plain files.

Out of scope: golden digest outputs (later beads add them).

title: Compaction cost: the summarising call is not in the transcript; estimate and show it
description:
A compaction makes one API call that reads the whole context and writes the summary. That
call is not written to the transcript: the compact_boundary record carries preTokens,
postTokens and durationMs but no usage, and the local history has no acompact agent file
(the model's agent kind `compact` covers versions that write one). So its cost is in Claude
Code's reported total only, inside "not explained by messages".

Measured on the local history (2026-10-02): 79 compactions in 44 sessions, all manual,
240k tokens before on average, 111 s each. Estimated from preTokens at the cache-read price
plus the summary at the output price: $0.27 median, $0.69 at most, $23 in total (if the
cache had expired the input side would cost far more: $135 at the uncached input price).
The first message after a compaction writes the new context to the cache; that one is in
the transcript: $32 over 73 compactions, $0.30 median.

To do: decide whether Compaction gets an estimated cost (clearly marked as an estimate,
never added to the recomputed total), and show per compaction what followed it (the
rewrite cost, which is real). Check against cost-state deltas across a compaction whether
the estimate holds.

title: Explorer 6.1: incremental reads for live sessions
description:
Read first: explorer/CLAUDE.md (rules), explorer/PLAN.md, explorer/docs/transcript-format.md.

Goal: avoid re-reading whole transcripts (largest seen: 52 MB) on every change to a live session. PLAN.md §6 "Incremental reads".

- The engine keeps, per live file, the Builder and the reader offset + guard. On change, read only the appended bytes when the guard matches; fall back to a full re-read on any mismatch, shrink, or parser-version change.
- Evict kept Builders when a session leaves the live set; bound total memory.
- Output must be byte-identical to a full rebuild.
acceptance_criteria: Property-style test: for each fixture, feeding the files in random chunk boundaries (on line breaks) through the incremental path yields a digest byte-identical to BuildSession. A rewritten file triggers a full re-read. Benchmark showing the per-update cost on a large synthetic file before and after. make test and make vet pass.

comments.author: Zsolt Terek
comments.text: Note from the reader task (merlin-t8s.4): the resume guard hashes only the 256 bytes before the offset, so an in-place rewrite that changes only earlier bytes and keeps the size (e.g. a same-length secret redaction) is NOT detected by OpenAt. The incremental path must therefore fall back to a full re-read whenever the file changed without growing (mtime changed, size equal or smaller), and should also do a full re-read when a session leaves the live set, so redactions always reach the digest.

comments.author: Zsolt Terek
comments.text:
Done. Design: the Claude harness keeps, per file of a *followed* session, the digest.Builder + reader offset/guard + size/mtime at read (internal/claude/incremental.go). Build for a followed session reads only appended bytes (OpenAt) and calls Builder.Result; digest.BuildSessionFrom (new, BuildSession is now a wrapper) takes the per-file reducer. Whole re-read of a file when: new, parser version differs, shrank, changed without growing (mtime moved, size not larger), guard mismatch. Unchanged file (size+mtime equal): not read. Partial last line is never consumed (Reader behaviour; harness-level test added).

Interface change (minimal, additive): optional harness.Follower {Follow(ref), Release(ref) (rebuild bool), SetLogf}. The daemon calls Follow when a session enters the live set and Release where it is deleted from it (internal/daemon/live.go); if Release says the stored digest came from appended reads it enqueues one priority build, which (session no longer followed) is a from-scratch full read. Engine, store, catalog untouched; Session unchanged. Sessions nobody follows (scan, first scan, idle rescan) never touch the cache.

Cap: 256 MiB of source bytes held (DefaultMaxHeldBytes), LRU by last build, evict on release and on exceeding the cap; bytes rather than count because a session is KBs..50 MB. Measured kept Builder heap ~0.7x source on a text-heavy synthetic transcript. Concurrency: one mutex on the maps, never held across file I/O; a session's state is checked out (busy) for the build; an overlapping build of the same session falls back to a plain full build.

Tests: property test over all fixtures x 5 fixed seeds x 7 steps (random line/mid-line cuts, digest compared as JSON with BuildSession at every step); fallback tests (guard, shrink, same-size+mtime, parser version, new file) assert full-read counts via IncrementalStats; partial line; Release/rebuild semantics; cap/eviction; concurrent use (-race); daemon test that a same-length edit hidden from the incremental path reaches the stored digest after the session leaves the live set (fails without the release). go test -race clean on claude, daemon, engine, harness; make test, make vet pass.

Benchmark (40 MB synthetic, ~1900 turns, 21 KB lines, one turn appended; M4 Max): full rebuild 268 ms, 272 MB allocated; incremental 0.91 ms, 2 MB; nothing changed 0.44 ms (~300x).

Real history (read-only, 6.5 min serve, 3355 sessions, 2 followed): first live build of the busy session read 29 files / 68 MB whole in 385 ms; its next 16 builds were incremental, 3.4 ms avg (max 6), 6.9 KB avg read. Scan afterwards (1.3 s): 3354 of 3355 digests identical by value; the 1 difference is the session being edited at the time (source files changed).
